title: Coach Lou's Big Pep Talk
text:
All right, team, gather around! Bring it in close.

Today is Sports Day, and I am so proud of you already. You ran laps, you stretched your {plural noun}, and you learned how to {verb} like champions. Keep your eyes on the ball and your feet on the {noun}. If you feel nervous, take a deep breath and think about {plural noun}.

The other team is very good too. Their coach says they eat {food} for breakfast every morning. That is fine. We have something even better. We have heart, and we have {adjective} socks. When you get out there, play {adverb}. Pass the ball, cheer for your friends, and if you hear me yell "{exclamation}!" that means run. Do not stop to {verb}.

Win or lose, we are going out for {adjective} pizza after the game. I will bring {number} juice boxes. Now put your hands in. On three, everybody shout "Go, {adjective} {plural noun}!"

title: Live from the Sack Race
text:
Hello, sports fans, and welcome to the big sack race at Oak Park Elementary! I am Ted, and here with me is my partner, Jill.

Thanks, Ted. What a {adjective} day for a race. The racers are climbing into their {plural noun}. The whistle blows! And they are off! Look at Mia in lane {number}. She is hopping {adverb}, Ted!

Yes, Jill, and look at Sam in lane three. He is not hopping at all. He is {verb ending in ing}. I have never seen that in a sack race before. The crowd is cheering {adverb}. Someone in the stands is waving a giant {noun}. And here comes the school {animal} onto the track!

Mia {past tense verb} across the finish line first, and Sam is right behind her. Everyone made it! All the racers will get a {color} ribbon and a cup of {food}. Coach Pat says it was the most {adjective} race in school history.

That is all from the sack race. Next up is the {adjective} relay. Do not {verb} away, folks!

title: Sports Day Schedule at Willow Creek
text:

9:00: Opening parade. Each class will march around the field holding a sign shaped like a {noun}. The kindergarten class will lead the way, walking very {adverb}. 9:30: Warm-ups with Coach Bea. We will touch our toes, shake our {plural noun}, and do {number} jumping jacks. 10:00: The three-legged race. Partners will tie their legs together and try to {verb} to the finish line.

10:45: Water break. Lemonade and {adjective} orange slices will be on the snack table. 11:00: The water balloon toss. Last year, Mr. Grant's balloon {past tense verb} right on his hat. He said it felt {adjective}. 11:30: Parents and teachers tug-of-war. The teachers have been practicing by pulling {plural noun} across the gym.

12:00: Picnic lunch on the grass. Bring a blanket, a {adjective} hat, and some {food}. Please do not feed your lunch to the {animal}. 12:30: Everyone gets a medal for {verb ending in ing}!

title: Official Rules of the Egg and Spoon Race
text:
Welcome to the egg and spoon race! Please read these rules.

Rule one: Each racer gets one spoon and one egg. The eggs are boiled, so they will not break. You may name your egg Eggbert or {silly word}. Rule two: Hold the spoon in your hand, not in your {body part}. You may hold it {adverb}, but you may not use glue, tape, or {plural noun}. Rule three: When the whistle blows, walk to the big {adjective} cone and back. You may not run. You may not {verb}. You may only walk, like a {animal}.

Rule four: If your egg falls, that is okay! Put it back on your spoon and keep {verb ending in ing}. Rule five: Cheer for every egg. A good cheer goes like this: "Go, egg, go! You are a {adjective} {noun}!"

Rule six: Every racer gets a sticker and a {noun}. The winner gets to {verb} first in the lunch line. Afterward, the eggs will become {food} sandwiches. Remember, the most important thing is to be {adjective}.

title: Dear Diary, Field Day Was Great
text:
Dear Diary,

Today was Field Day, the best day of the whole year. I wore my team shirt, which is bright {color} and has a {noun} on the front. First was the hula hoop contest. I kept my hoop spinning for {number} seconds. My friend Leo kept his hoop going while he {past tense verb} at the same time. Everybody clapped {adverb}.

Next was the obstacle course. We had to crawl under a net, hop through tires, and {verb} over a pile of {plural noun}. I went as fast as a {animal} and made it to the end. At lunch, Mom brought a cooler full of {adjective} snacks, like grapes and {plural noun}. Then we watched the teachers race. Mr. Kim ran so fast his whistle started {verb ending in ing}.

At the end of the day, everyone got a ribbon. Mine says "Most {adjective} Hopper." I am going to hang it above my bed next to my {noun}.

title: How to Do the Blue Team Cheer
text:
Welcome to the Blue Team! Our cheer is the best. Here is how to do it.

Step one: Stand in a line with your teammates. Put your hands on your hips and look very {adjective}. Step two: Stomp your feet {number} times, like a herd of {plural noun}. Step three: Clap your hands over your head and shout, "We are Blue, we are true, we can {verb} and so can you!"

Step four: Spin around once, then hold on to your {noun}. Step five: Wiggle your {body part} and say "{silly word}" as {adverb} as you can. Step six: Jump up high and pretend you are a {adjective} rocket. Step seven: Give a high five to the person next to you and say, "Nice {verb ending in ing}!" Step eight: Take a bow and toss a few {plural noun} into the air.

Coach Mae says if we do our cheer every morning, we will feel {adjective} all day long. Last year, the Red Team {past tense verb} when they heard it.

title: The Sports Day Awards
text:
Good afternoon, families! Thank you for coming to the Sports Day Awards. Every student worked hard today, so every student gets an award and a {adjective} ribbon.

The Super Sprinter Award goes to Jada, who ran so {adverb} that her shoelaces came untied. The Best Teammate Award goes to Marco, who cheered for everyone and shared his {plural noun} with the whole class. The Golden Spoon Award goes to Ellie. She carried her egg all the way to the finish line on a {noun}.

The Big Jump Award goes to Omar. He jumped {number} feet and landed like a {adjective} {animal}. The Sunshine Award goes to Ms. Wu, who stood at the finish line all day {verb ending in ing}. The Silly Hat Award goes to Principal Green. His hat had {plural noun} glued all over it, and it {past tense verb} every time he moved.

Thank you all for a {adjective} day. Next year, we will add a new event: the {adjective} {noun} relay. Please practice at home!

title: Snack Table Sign-Up Sheet
text:

Granola bars: Any kind is fine, as long as there are no {plural noun} inside. Sunscreen: Mr. Tate puts it on his nose, his ears, and his {body part}.

title: Please Pick Me for Team Mascot
text:
Dear Coach Rivera,

My name is Nora. I want to be the Green Team mascot on Sports Day. I would be a great mascot because I am {adjective}. I can cheer loudly, dance {adverb}, and do a cartwheel almost every time.

My costume is a giant {animal} suit that my grandma made. It has a long tail and {number} fuzzy {plural noun} on the back. It is a little bit smelly, but only on hot days.

As the mascot, I will run up and down the field and help the team {verb}. When our team scores, I will do my special dance, called the {silly word}. When the other team scores, I will clap for them too. I have been practicing my mascot noises. My best one sounds like a {adjective} {noun} {verb ending in ing}.

I promise to be {adjective} and to never take off my {noun} during the game.

Your friend,
Nora

title: Tug-of-War Ends in a Tie
text:
This is Ruby Wells with the Sports Day news.

Today at Elm Street School, the tug-of-war between the Red Team and the Yellow Team ended in a tie for the first time in {number} years. Both teams grabbed the rope and pulled {adverb}. The crowd cheered so loudly that a {noun} fell off the bleachers.

For ten whole minutes, nobody moved. The Red Team pulled. The Yellow Team pulled. A {adjective} squirrel sat in the middle of the field and ate {plural noun}. Then both teams started {verb ending in ing} at the same time. They laughed so hard they all sat down on the {adjective} grass.

The referee, Mr. Ito, {past tense verb} and blew his whistle. He said it was the most {adjective} match he had ever seen. After the game, both teams shared a big bowl of {plural noun} and promised to {verb} again next year. Mr. Ito says he will bring a longer rope and a {noun}.

Reporting live, this is Ruby Wells. Back to you, {name}.
